Reducing mucus viscosity

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 52-year-old man with bronchiectasis has tenacious sputum despite an established airway-clearance regimen. A nebulized adjunct reduces the viscosity of a collected sputum sample without degrading its DNA. Which molecular action best identifies the effect of acetylcysteine?

  1. Hydrolysis of extracellular DNA phosphodiester bonds
  2. Competitive inhibition of muscarinic receptors
  3. Stimulation of beta2 receptors on smooth muscle
  4. Blockade of central opioid receptors
  5. Disruption of disulfide bonds in mucus proteins
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Disruption of disulfide bonds in mucus proteins

The sulfhydryl group of acetylcysteine disrupts disulfide linkages in mucus, reducing viscosity.

Understanding the options

Disruption of disulfide bonds in mucus proteins
Reducing these protein cross-links promotes mucolysis.
Hydrolysis of extracellular DNA phosphodiester bonds
DNA hydrolysis is the action of dornase alfa rather than acetylcysteine.
Competitive inhibition of muscarinic receptors
Muscarinic antagonism affects airway tone and secretions, not mucus disulfide bonds.
Stimulation of beta2 receptors on smooth muscle
Beta2 stimulation relaxes airway smooth muscle.
Blockade of central opioid receptors
Central opioid receptor blockade does not explain the ex vivo sputum effect.
